newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Benco diamond mine ship Moonstar sets sail.
newsitem.headline: Benco diamond mine ship Moonstar sets sail.

text.p: Benguela Concessions Ltd's (Benco) 45 million rand Moonstar floating mine was due to leave Cape Town harbour on Thursday to prepare for its first diamond mining operations off the South African west coast.
Managing director Stuart Smith told Reuters that the Moonstar, a joint venture with Australia's Moonstone Diamond Corporation NL, would first undertake ore body work before starting to mine.
"She is taking bunkers now and is due to sail this afternoon up to Concession 2b, adjacent to Port Nolloth," Stuart said.

"By the new year we should start on the systematic ore body development work to make sure that when we start mining we do not sterilise fertile ground by dumping tailings on top of it. We will start mining in earnest in February," Stuart said.
The Moonstar, which features the latest technology in marine diamond mining, was commissioned in October by South African Minerals and Energy Affairs Minister Penuell Maduna.
It has undergone sea trials this last month.
When mining, the Moonstar is expected to operate 24 hours a day and produce up to 65,000 carats worth of marine diamonds a year in Concessions 2b and 3b.
The floating mine is expected to generate a gross annual income of around $13 million.
The deposits in the concessions were identified during a drilling programme carried out by Benco's joint venture in 1994 with giant Australian mining company BHP (The Broken Hill Proprietary Co).
BHP pulled out because it considered the diamond finds too small. Moonstone then joined Benco, providing the mining vessel.
The ship will stay at sea for at least a year and crew changes and fresh provisions will be flown to it by helicopter.
